scenarios.title: Repair the drivers available before the root filesystem
scenarios.summary: Use saved driver choices and dracut to repair an initramfs that cannot reach its root disk.
scenarios.objective: Save the driver-selection fragment and regenerate early userspace for supplied kernel 6.6.61. Make the selected candidate reach the supplied NVMe/ext4 root and keep every working fallback file unchanged.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read each failed result: saved fragment, selected kernel, actual image contents, root handoff and protected fallback are checked separately.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: The kernel needs early drivers before it can reach the main filesystem.
guide.action: Read the worked example and supplied generic profile; the required kernel and module inputs are already prepared.

guide.title: Investigate the separate example
guide.why: A filename and a generation message do not prove the right drivers or kernel were selected.
guide.action: Use the example editor and console. Save changes, inspect the represented contents with lsinitrd and check the actual entry.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: The selected files and preserved fallback determine the result.
guide.action: Use the assignment’s supplied values; save any changed fragment or entry, regenerate the intended image and select Check configuration.

scenarios.explanation: An initramfs provides early userspace before the main filesystem is available. This supplied generic profile includes the prepared NVMe/ext4 drivers unless the saved fragment omits them. Saving configuration does not rebuild an existing image. Inspecting the image and testing the selected entry connect driver choices to the actual modeled root handoff. Different literal edits and supported command forms are accepted; the fallback remains unchanged.
hints: Inspect the image named in the candidate’s initrd line; compare its Kernel line and driver files with the supplied target.
Save the fragment before generating. In dracut, --kver selects a kernel; -k is a different, unsupported module-directory option.
+= appends text; appending an empty string does not remove an existing omission. Change or remove the omission, save, then regenerate.
scenarios.simplifications: Supplied generic baseline hostonly=no, prepared NVMe/ext4 kernel/module records and five driver names only. Literal omit_drivers assignments/comments; no general dracut.conf shell evaluation. Explicit kernel/output dracut and limited lsinitrd driver-file inventory, not real archive data. No host discovery, feature modules, compression, hooks, privilege checks, C compilation, firmware, actual tools or boot. mkinitrd/mkinitramfs remain unsupported. All paths, files and root/init checks are simulated.

scenarios.explanation: The entry selects a kernel and one or more early-userspace images. Their internal release and supplied build identities must agree; a version-looking filename is not evidence. You can rebuild the selected image in place with force, or create a different image and save an entry that selects it. The checks follow the actual selected files and preserve the working fallback, rather than requiring one command transcript.
hints: Inspect the image named in the candidate’s initrd line; compare its Kernel line and driver files with the supplied target.
Save the fragment before generating. In dracut, --kver selects a kernel; -k is a different, unsupported module-directory option.
A new unselected image cannot repair an entry that still points to a wrong image. Rebuild the selected output with force, or save an entry selecting your new output.
scenarios.simplifications: Supplied generic baseline hostonly=no, prepared NVMe/ext4 kernel/module records and five driver names only. Literal omit_drivers assignments/comments; no general dracut.conf shell evaluation. Explicit kernel/output dracut and limited lsinitrd driver-file inventory, not real archive data.
